_method: Benign apps from F-Droid (not vulnerable by design), used for the false-positive rate. There is no documented vulnerability list, so every category the scanner reports is labelled in 'reviewed' after checking its evidence: true = the weakness is really there, false = a false alarm. Recall is not measured on this set.
_notes: Rules were not changed after this run.
A true label means the code or configuration really has the weakness; it does not mean the app is unsafe to use.

Noisiest rules on benign apps: HTTP-ENDPOINT (URLs inside bundled JavaScript and hint strings), STORAGE-EXTERNAL (path lookups, not writes) and EXPORTED-COMPONENT (intended entry points such as widgets).

Exported Components.note: Exported on purpose as intent entry points (scan, pick, share, settings); no weakness shown

HTTP Endpoints.note: Input hints, code that prefixes user-typed URLs with http://, and app-link hosts; no endpoint the app calls

Cleartext Traffic.note: android:usesCleartextTraffic=true (lets users send scans to their own http:// URLs)

Insecure Data Storage.note: android:allowBackup=true; the Downloads writes are user-initiated exports

Insecure Cryptography.note: MD5/SHA-1 only display hashes of scanned content, not a security use

Exported Components.note: Notification receivers and PFABackupService are exported without a permission, so any app can reach them

Insecure WebView.note: The document view enables JavaScript and file access and exposes addJavascriptInterface to rendered content

Exported Components.note: Widget providers, widget configuration and document-open entry points must be exported

Hardcoded Secrets.note: hidden_password = **** is a UI mask, not a secret

HTTP Endpoints.note: All 32 hits are URLs inside bundled JS libraries, an autolink prefix and XML feature names

Insecure Data Storage.note: android:allowBackup=true; the external-storage hits are mostly path lookups for user-chosen folders
